title: Parity and Symmetry of the Product of Two Odd Functions
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
question: Suppose f(x) and g(x) are both odd functions defined on the entire real line. What can be definitively concluded regarding the symmetry and parity of the product function h(x) = f(x)g(x)?

options.text: h(x) is an even function with y-axis symmetry
options.explanation: Correct! Evaluating h(-x) = f(-x)g(-x) = [-f(x)][-g(x)] = f(x)g(x) = h(x). Because h(-x) = h(x), the product is an even function and its graph is symmetric across the y-axis.

options.text: h(x) is an odd function with origin symmetry
options.explanation: Incorrect. Multiplying two negative factors yields a positive product, producing even parity rather than odd.
options.misconception: Student uses additive thinking ('odd plus odd is odd, so odd times odd must be odd'), confusing the addition of odd functions with their algebraic product.

options.text: h(x) is neither even nor odd
options.explanation: Incorrect. The product of two odd functions always possesses definite even symmetry.
options.misconception: Student assumes that multiplying two symmetric functions destroys their symmetry properties, failing to carry out the algebraic sign test h(-x) = (-f(x))(-g(x)).

options.text: h(x) is both even and odd
options.explanation: Incorrect. The only function that is both even and odd on R is the zero function, but the product of two arbitrary non-zero odd functions is not identically zero.
options.misconception: Student confuses parity product rules with the zero function, falsely believing that combining two symmetries causes the function to vanish identically.

explanation: By definition of odd functions, f(-x) = -f(x) and g(-x) = -g(x). For the product function h(x) = f(x)g(x), we evaluate h(-x) = f(-x)g(-x) = (-f(x))(-g(x)) = f(x)g(x) = h(x). Since h(-x) = h(x) for all x, h is an even function with y-axis reflection symmetry.
